Oracle Frontier section, theorem discussion: the text says the result is a “transported analogue of weak-IV robust ratio inference,” but the comparison to classical weak-IV work would be sharper if it stated that the novelty is the effective-strength replacement n mu_n^2/kappa_n under the stated transport geometry; add one sentence tying this directly to the cited weak-IV frontier literature.

Finite-cell section: the sample-only finite-cell result is presented as broadly feasible, but its uniform source-cell probabilities and balanced propensity are strong design restrictions; add a paragraph after the finite-cell theorem interpreting this as a constructive benchmark and distinguishing it from the regular-cell extension with known q_x,n and e_x,n.

Related Literature and Discussion, final paragraph: the synthesis is clear but underplays the role of compact parameter-space length in the expected-length frontier; add a sentence explaining that bounded outcomes and binary receipt make Lebesgue length on Theta the risk scale used throughout.

Proof appendix: the prose is unusually long for a paper whose formal results are machine verified, and it sometimes repeats theorem-level conditions; consider moving proof-step narration that mainly mirrors Lean bookkeeping into a shorter verification appendix while keeping the econometric proof ideas prominent.

The abstract and introduction present the frontier as "the oracle minimax expected length above threshold $t_0$ is characterized up to constants as $\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}$," but \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} delivers only the lower bound over $\mathcal P_n$ and $\mathcal N_n$, while the matching upper bound in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment} requires the additional existence of an admissible geometry $\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G$ satisfying \cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}, and the constants $c_\alpha,C_\alpha$ differ by an $\varepsilon$- and $\alpha$-dependent factor that is never quantified. Fix: in the abstract and in the paragraph containing "$V^\star(t_0)\asymp\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}$", state the two-sided bound with its explicit constants $c_\alpha=3(1-\alpha)^2/16$ and $C_\alpha=\max\{2,4L_\alpha+8/\varepsilon^2\}$, name the admissible-geometry hypothesis as a condition of the upper bound, and note that the constant ratio grows like $\alpha^{-1/2}\varepsilon^{-2}$ so the characterization is a rate statement, not a sharp-constant one.

The uniformity claim is stated more strongly in prose than the theorem supports. The introduction says "the lower bound applies uniformly across ways of producing a given $t_0$", and the discussion after \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} says the bound applies "whether weak identification comes from a small complier share, highly dispersed transport weights, or any combination producing the same value of $n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n$" — but the proof of \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} constructs a single geometry with $w_n\equiv1$, $\kappa_n=1$, and $e_n\equiv1/2$, i.e. the *no-dispersion* configuration, and obtains uniformity only because the lower bound never depends on the decomposition. Fix: replace the two sentences with an accurate affirmative formulation such as "the lower-bound constant depends on $(c,\varepsilon,\alpha)$ alone and is therefore valid at every $(\mu_n,\kappa_n)$ pair with $n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n=t_0$", and add a remark noting that the witness attaining the bound uses unit weights, so the statement is that dispersion cannot *help*, not that a dispersed witness is exhibited.

\Cref{obj:ass:receipt-transport} is materially weaker than \cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport} — conditional transport for the outcome contrast versus only target-average transport for the receipt contrast — and the paper asserts this asymmetry "matches the estimand" without discussing what it rules out or how a practitioner would assess either condition. Neither assumption is compared to the standard mean-exchangeability-over-$S$ conditions in \citet{Dahabreh2020} or \citet{ChenHuang2025}, and no example of a violation is given. Fix: after the paragraph beginning "Together, \cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport} supply the exact contrast structure", add a paragraph giving (i) a concrete data-generating example in which conditional outcome-contrast transport holds but selection is on unobserved compliance intensity so the conclusion fails, (ii) an explicit statement of which conditional-transport conditions in the cited transportability literature imply each of the two assumptions, and (iii) a sentence on what evidence would support the target-average form in an application.

The array conditions in \cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array} are stated but their joint restrictiveness is left uninterpreted: $w\le 2k_n$ with $\kappa_n\le k_n$ and $k_n=o(n^{1/2})$ together cap the effective sample size $n/\kappa_n$ from below at order $n^{1/2}$, and $\mu_n\to0$ is imposed as a modelling regime rather than derived. As written a reader cannot tell whether $t_n$ can be held fixed at a given $t_0$ along the array, which is exactly what \cref{obj:def:frontier-risk} requires. Fix: after \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}, add a remark that traces one explicit admissible sequence — for instance $k_n=n^{1/3}$, $\kappa_n\asymp k_n$, $\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\asymp n^{-1/3}$ — verifying every condition and confirming $t_n\equiv t_0$, and state plainly which empirically relevant configurations the $o(n^{1/2})$ gate excludes.

The finite-cell results are described in the introduction as procedures that "serve as constructive attainability benchmarks", but \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source} forces a uniform $k_n$-cell source design with $e(X)\equiv1/2$, and \cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} additionally treats $(q_{x,n})$ and $(e_{x,n})$ as known inputs by \cref{obj:def:regular-cell-feasible-honesty} — so neither construction is feasible in the sense a reader of an applied econometrics paper would assume. The label "sample-only" for the $\mathcal N_n$ rule is accurate only because the design constants are absorbed into the model class. Fix: rewrite the introductory sentence and the paragraph opening "We next replace oracle weights by cell-frequency estimates" to state affirmatively which inputs each procedure consumes (target covariate sample and source sample under a known uniform design for $\mathcal N_n$; additionally known $(q_{x,n},e_{x,n})$ for $\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}$), and add one sentence identifying the estimation of $(q_{x,n},e_{x,n})$ as the remaining step in a clearly labelled limitations or future-work paragraph.

Positioning is bibliographically broad but analytically thin: the Related Literature section lists roughly forty references in undifferentiated strings such as "\citep{GleserHwang1987,Dufour1997,BoundJaegerBaker1995,StaigerStock1997,...}" without identifying which prior result the present frontier extends, and the closest comparison — the single-population expected-length results behind \citet{Dufour1997} and \citet{StockWrightYogo2002} — is never stated as a theorem so the reader cannot see that \cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction} recovers it. Similarly \citet{ChenHuang2025} is cited five times as motivation for the transport conditions but its estimand and assumptions are never stated. Fix: replace the two longest citation strings with two or three sentences that state the specific prior result (target parameter, assumptions, rate) and the exact delta contributed here, and add a short paragraph after \cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction} making the recovery of the known $w\equiv1$ benchmark explicit.

Introduction, paragraph beginning “The main oracle result characterizes…”: the phrase “for each fixed positive threshold t_0” is broader than several theorem statements that also require fixed overlap, dominated transport, envelope and second-moment control, and sub-root cell growth; revise the topic sentence to state those gates before the rate claim.

Abstract and introduction: “uniform over decompositions of t_0 into weak transported compliance and covariate-weight dispersion” is an important claim but reads slightly stronger than the displayed formal statements because the constants also depend on overlap, sampling ratio, and alpha; add a short qualifier such as “within the stated overlap, sampling-ratio, envelope, and dispersion class.”

Setup section: the assumptions are clearly listed, but their restrictiveness is mostly interpreted locally rather than synthesized; add one paragraph after the model-class definition explaining the substantive meaning of conditional outcome-contrast transport, target-average receipt transport, fixed instrument overlap, and k_n=o(n^{1/2}) as the operating domain of the paper.

Finite-cell section: the sample-only claim for the uniform finite-cell rule is useful, but the regular-cell rule’s known source-cell probabilities and known propensities are a substantial information condition; foreground this distinction in the paragraph introducing the regular-cell construction.

Related literature: several citation clusters are broad lists, especially in the transportability and weak-IV paragraphs; tighten by naming the exact connection for two or three key references and moving the rest into supporting citations.

Appendix verification note: “formal theorem statements and their proofs are verified in Lean 4” is strong and helpful, but readers need a precise boundary; add a sentence specifying that econometric modeling choices, citations, and manuscript exposition remain outside the machine-checked layer.

Abstract and Introduction advertise the rate as a frontier in the effective-strength scalar t_n = n mu_n^2 / kappa_n, but every displayed bound is a two-sided order in the FIXED THRESHOLD t_0 with constants c_alpha = 3(1-alpha)^2/16 and C_alpha = max{2, 4L_alpha + 8/eps^2}. The ratio C_alpha/c_alpha blows up as eps -> 0 or alpha -> 1, so 'asymp' hides a gap that is not uniform in the overlap constant. Fix: in the abstract, state 'up to constants depending on (c, eps, alpha)' as is already done, and add one sentence after Theorem obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment reporting the explicit constant ratio and noting that the characterization is an order statement at fixed (eps, alpha), not a sharp-constant result.

The lower bound is witnessed entirely at unit transport weight (w = 1, kappa_n = 1), as the proof of obj:thm:oracle-converse makes explicit, yet the Introduction claims the converse shows 'how these two features jointly determine' expected length and that t_n 'combines first-stage strength and weight dispersion'. A converse attained on the no-dispersion slice establishes only that the reciprocal-square-root rate in t_0 is unimprovable; it does not establish that kappa_n is the correct dispersion index, since any index equal to 1 at w = 1 would pass the same test. Fix: rewrite the Introduction paragraph beginning 'The main oracle result' to state that the converse is witnessed on the unit-weight slice and that kappa_n enters the characterization through the upper bound (obj:def:inversion-handle radius) and through the least-favorable calibration p_n(x) = mu_n w(x)/kappa_n in obj:def:least-favorable-witness, rather than through a dispersion-separating converse.

Assumption obj:ass:receipt-transport is stated as an equality of TARGET-population averages of the conditional receipt contrast, which is markedly weaker than the conditional transport imposed on the outcome contrast in obj:ass:outcome-transport, but the paper never discusses what this asymmetry rules in or out. The paragraph beginning 'Together, cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport}' asserts the asymmetry 'matches the estimand' without argument. Fix: add two or three sentences giving a substantive example where the integrated receipt condition holds while the conditional version fails (e.g. compensating heterogeneity in compliance across covariate strata), and state plainly that the integrated form suffices only because the denominator mu_n enters as a single target average.

Assumption obj:ass:degrading-array requires mu_n -> 0 as a MODEL-CLASS condition, so P_n contains only arrays with vanishing transported first stage; but the frontier risk in obj:def:frontier-risk supremizes over P in P_n with t_n >= t_0, and obj:thm:oracle-converse also asserts a bound for t_0 in (0, t_c] with t_c = 1. The interaction between a shrinking mu_n, a growing kappa_n <= k_n = o(n^{1/2}), and a fixed positive t_0 constrains which decompositions are actually populated, yet the paper claims constants 'apply uniformly over all decompositions of the effective strength t_0 into mu_n and kappa_n'. Fix: add a remark after obj:ass:degrading-array showing explicitly which (mu_n, kappa_n) pairs satisfy both mu_n -> 0 and n mu_n^2 / kappa_n >= t_0 under kappa_n <= k_n = o(n^{1/2}), so the reader can see the populated region is nonempty and what it excludes.

The finite-cell results are repeatedly described as attaining 'the oracle frontier order', but the oracle benchmark V*(t_0) is defined over the full class P_n while the feasible bounds in obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment and obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment are stated over N_n and N_n^reg with DIFFERENT constants (C_0 = max{2, 4 sqrt2 L_{alpha,c} + 8 B_c} with B_c = 32(1 + 1/c), versus the oracle max{2, 4 L_alpha + 8/eps^2}). The uniform finite-cell class also fixes e(X) = 1/2 and uniform cell masses, and the regular-cell procedure additionally consumes known q_{x,n} and e_{x,n}. Fix: replace 'attain the same expected-length order as the oracle benchmark' in the Introduction and in the paragraph after obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment with a precise statement naming the class, the required known inputs, and the constant, and add one sentence stating that the constant degrades in c through B_c = 32(1 + 1/c).

Positioning relative to ChenHuang2025 is asserted five times ('follows the contrast-and-weighting logic', 'the closest transported-noncompliance papers') without ever stating what that paper establishes or how the present transport conditions differ from its. Similarly, ArmstrongKolesar2021 is cited only inside the Verification note, where it plays no role, and several references (Ross2026, Aronow2026, Ren2025, Rudolph2025, SmuclerLanniMasip2025, Ma2023) appear only in undifferentiated citation lists. Fix: in the Related Literature section, add one sentence per closest paper stating its estimand, its identification conditions, and the precise point of contact or departure (in particular whether ChenHuang2025 imposes conditional or integrated receipt transport), and either move ArmstrongKolesar2021 to a use site or drop it.

The Appendix section titled 'Proofs, Auxiliary Arguments, and Verification Note' contains only proof SKETCHES, while the actual proofs appear in a separate later section labelled sec:deferred-proofs, and the Introduction's final sentence points readers to sec:deferred-proofs for 'the Lean 4 verification scope' — which is in the earlier appendix, not in sec:deferred-proofs. Fix: merge the two appendix sections or retitle the first as a proof-strategy overview, and repoint the Introduction sentence to the appendix section that actually carries the verification note.

Abstract: the phrase "sample-based confidence sets with the same expected-length order" compresses important gates; revise to state "in uniform finite-cell and regular-cell classes satisfying the stated cell-growth, overlap, sampling-ratio, and known-input conditions" so the abstract matches the formal theorems.

Introduction, paragraph beginning "The main oracle result characterizes": the phrase "row-rate condition k_n=o(n^{1/2})" is opaque before k_n is tied to both envelope scale and cell scale; add one sentence explaining that k_n controls the transport-weight envelope and, in cell models, the number of cells.

Oracle Frontier section: the lower-bound discussion says the converse is witnessed at unit transport weight, but the later fixed-geometry least-favorable construction emphasizes complier mass loaded toward target-heavy cells; add a clarifying bridge distinguishing the global converse slice from the fixed-geometry calibration.

Finite-cell section after \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment}: the implementation paragraph mixes theorem interpretation with procedural instructions and repeats material from the theorem; tighten it into a short interpretive paragraph focused on why the collision statistic estimates the relevant dispersion scale.

Related Literature: several 2025-2026 working-paper citations are listed in clusters without saying what each contributes; add brief parenthetical roles for ChenHuang2025, ZengKennedyBodnarNaimi2024, Ross2026, Aronow2026, and Ren2025, or reduce the list to the most directly connected papers.

Assumption discussion throughout Setup: assumptions are individually interpreted, but their joint restrictiveness is underdeveloped; add a clearly titled Limitations or Scope paragraph covering bounded outcomes, binary receipt, fixed overlap, domination, and k_n=o(n^{1/2}) as the domain of the results.

The abstract and Introduction both state the two-sided characterization \(V^\star(t_0)\asymp\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\) as if it were a genuine minimax frontier over the transported class, but \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} obtains the converse entirely from the unit-weight slice \(w=1\), where \(\kappa_n=1\) and \(t_n=n\mu_n^2\) by \cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction}. Nothing in the lower bound is driven by weight dispersion, so the claim that the two effects 'jointly determine' expected length and 'combine in the single scalar \(t_n\)' is stronger than what is proved: only the upper bound uses \(\kappa_n\), and the sentence 'The same constants \(c_0\) and \(t_c\) apply uniformly over all decompositions of the effective strength \(t_0\) into \(\mu_n\) and \(\kappa_n\)' is a statement about constants, not evidence that \(\kappa_n\) is the correct dispersion index. Fix: in the Introduction paragraph beginning 'The main oracle result characterizes...' and in the abstract, state affirmatively that the converse is established on the no-shift slice and that the matching upper bound holds uniformly in \(\kappa_n\), so \(t_n\) is shown to be a sufficient index for attainment; add a remark after \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} recording that a converse witnessed at nondegenerate weight dispersion is established by the fixed-geometry result \cref{obj:thm:fixed-geometry-frontier} uniformly over \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\), and make explicit which of the two statements carries the dispersion content.

The Introduction and Section 3 describe \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} and \cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} as showing that 'feasible' procedures attain the oracle order, but the two constructions require very different information and the prose blurs this. The uniform finite-cell rule is genuinely sample-only, yet it rests on \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}, which fixes \(e(X)=1/2\) exactly and imposes exactly uniform cell masses \(1/k_n\) — a design assumption, not an estimation result. The regular-cell rule relaxes uniformity but takes \((q_{x,n})\) and \((e_{x,n})\) as known inputs per \cref{obj:def:regular-cell-feasible-honesty}. Neither delivers feasibility in the sense a reader of the phrase 'feasible cell weight learning' (Section 3 title) will expect. Fix: retitle Section 3 to name the information structure (e.g. 'Fixed Geometry and Cell-Design Attainability Benchmarks'), and in the Introduction sentence beginning 'Finally, \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment,...}' state in one clause exactly what each rule consumes: known cell partition with balanced encouragement and uniform masses for \(\mathcal N_n\); known partition, known \(q_{x,n}\), and known \(e_{x,n}\) for \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

The assumption commentary is uniformly descriptive rather than evaluative: each of \cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:transport-domination,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array} is followed by one or two sentences restating what the condition does, with no discussion of when it fails, what it rules out, or how it compares to the transport conditions in the cited literature. The asymmetry between conditional outcome-contrast transport and target-average receipt-contrast transport is the paper's most distinctive modelling choice, and the paragraph beginning 'Together, \cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport} supply the exact contrast structure' explains the algebraic role of the asymmetry without asking whether the weaker integrated receipt condition is substantively plausible in encouragement designs where compliance varies systematically with the covariates that drive transport. Fix: add a paragraph after that one giving one concrete design in which conditional outcome-contrast transport is credible while conditional receipt-contrast transport fails, and stating what \cref{obj:ass:receipt-transport} does allow (site-varying compliance that averages to the same target-population complier share) versus what it excludes.

\cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array} tie the pointwise weight bound \(2k_n\), the second-moment bound \(\kappa_n\le k_n\), and the cell count to a single scale \(k_n\), and the text calls this 'the same scale that appears in the finite-cell construction' without justifying the coupling. In particular \(\kappa_n\le k_n\) is what makes \(t_n=n\mu_n^2/\kappa_n\) a nondegenerate index, and \(k_n=o(n^{1/2})\) is what keeps cell learning on the score scale; the reader is not told which conclusions survive if the envelope and the dispersion bound are decoupled into separate rates. Fix: after \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}, add two sentences identifying which results use only \(\kappa_n\le k_n\) (the oracle upper bound in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment}) and which additionally need \(k_n=o(n^{1/2})\) as a cell count (the finite-cell results and the empirical-Kish lower-tail bound \(\Pr\{K_n<\kappa_n/2\}\le 16k_n^2/n\) used in the coverage step), so the single-scale convention is visibly a simplification rather than a structural requirement.

The paragraph in Section 3 beginning 'For implementation on the uniform-cell benchmark, the inputs are...' reads as practitioner guidance but has no bridge to any data-analytic setting: the paper offers no worked example, no numerical illustration of how large \(t_0\) must be before \(t_0^{-1/2}\) beats the trivial length \(2\), and no guidance on how an applied user would assess whether \(k_n=o(n^{1/2})\) or \(\kappa_n\le k_n\) is plausible for their target sample. Given that \(C_0=\max\{2,4L_\alpha+8/\varepsilon^2\}\) with \(L_\alpha=(8/\alpha\varepsilon^2)^{1/2}\), the upper bound is uninformative relative to the trivial set \(\Theta\) until \(t_0\) is quite large — for \(\alpha=0.05,\varepsilon=0.1\) the constant exceeds 800. Fix: add a short remark after \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment} tabulating \(C_0\) at two or three \((\alpha,\varepsilon)\) pairs and stating the effective-strength range over which the bound improves on length \(2\), so readers can calibrate the rate statement against the constants actually delivered.

Two cross-reference and structure defects will confuse readers. First, the Introduction's final sentence says '\Cref{sec:deferred-proofs} records the Lean 4 verification scope', but the verification note is a \paragraph inside the preceding appendix section, while \label{sec:deferred-proofs} is attached to the section titled 'Proofs of the main results' — the pointer lands on the wrong target. Second, \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} and \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} both introduce the symbol \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) and both restate \(\mu_n=(t_0\kappa_n/n)^{1/2}\) and \(p_n(x)=\mu_n w(x)/\kappa_n\), and \cref{obj:synth_5} restates the same construction a third time; the reader cannot tell which is the definition and which is the derived separation bound, especially since \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} is stated as a definition but its content is a pair of inequalities. Fix: move \label{sec:deferred-proofs} to the appendix section containing the verification note (or repoint the Introduction sentence at the correct section), and merge \cref{obj:synth_5} into \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} while restating \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} as a lemma or remark whose displayed \(\chi^2\) and TV bounds are labelled as consequences of the family just defined.

Introduction, paragraph beginning “The main oracle result characterizes”: the phrase “the upper-rate comparison uses t_n as the common scale” is weaker and less direct than the surrounding result statement; replace with a concise positive theorem summary that states the exact class and the two-sided order once, then move repeated gates to a parenthetical.

Setup, discussion after `def:model-class`: the assumption discussion motivates each restriction mechanically but gives little economic interpretation of target-average receipt transport versus conditional outcome transport; add two or three sentences explaining what empirical invariance each condition encodes and when a design would plausibly satisfy it.

Oracle Frontier, `thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment`: the prose says the target covariate sample remains part of the two-sample experiment, but the displayed oracle score is source-sample only; clarify that target-sample randomness enters the risk experiment and feasible procedures, while this oracle statistic uses target information only through declared `w`.

Fixed Geometry section: the least-favorable construction is introduced as calibrating compliers toward target-heavy covariate values, but the prose does not spell out why `p_n(x)=mu_n w(x)/kappa_n` preserves the first-stage and creates the `kappa_n` variance scale; add a short explanatory derivation before or after `def:least-favorable-witness`.

Related Literature: the paragraph listing recent transported-noncompliance and weak-IV extrapolation work is dense and somewhat citation-like; split it into narrower claims, e.g. transported CACE identification, weak-IV robust two-sample inference, and transported ATE minimaxity, with each citation group tied to one specific role.

Appendix verification note: “The Lean-checked layer covers…” is useful, but it risks sounding broader than reader-visible proof obligations; revise to state exactly which formal statements are checked and that econometric interpretation and citation positioning are supplied by the manuscript prose.

Abstract and introduction assert that the frontier is "characterized" and that oracle procedures "have minimax expected length of order min{1, t_0^{-1/2}}", but the two-sided matching statement in the full class \mathcal P_n is assembled from a lower bound proved on a unit-weight finite-cell slice (\Cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse}, whose proof takes P_{S,n}^X = P_{T,n} = uniform, w \equiv 1, e \equiv 1/2) and an upper bound proved over \mathcal P_n. The abstract's sentence "The unit-transport-weight least-favorable slice is embedded in the transported class, so its weak-ratio lower bound applies to the larger transported model" is accurate, but the surrounding prose ("The paper characterizes the oracle minimax expected-length frontier", "the oracle minimax expected length is characterized, up to constants") overstates what a lower bound witnessed at \kappa_n = 1 establishes about the role of transport dispersion. Fix: in the abstract and in the paragraph after \Cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment}, state that the matching constants are attained with the lower-bound witness having unit weight, and say explicitly that the \kappa_n-dependence in the frontier is established through the upper bound and the fixed-geometry family of \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness}, not through a dispersed-weight converse.

The paper's headline interpretation — that first-stage weakness and transport dispersion "enter through a common scale" and are treated "symmetrically" — is asserted three times (introduction final paragraph; end of the oracle section; end of the fixed-geometry section) but never supported by an argument that the pair (\mu_n, \kappa_n) is not separately identified in the risk. The uniformity clause of \Cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} ("The same constants c_0 and t_c apply uniformly over all decompositions of the effective strength t_0") is a statement about constants, not about the value function; it does not preclude a procedure exploiting \kappa_n separately. Fix: replace "treats a weak transported first stage and high transport dispersion symmetrically" with a claim tied to what is proved, e.g. "the two-sided bounds depend on (\mu_n, \kappa_n) only through t_n, so no admissible split of a given t_0 changes the order", and delete the stronger symmetry reading.

\Cref{obj:ass:receipt-transport} is the paper's most substantive and least standard restriction — it equates a target-law average of a cross-population receipt contrast, an assumption not testable from the source experiment plus target covariates alone — yet it is glossed as "the standard" condition with a single citation, in the same register used for randomization, exclusion, and monotonicity. The clinic-rollout paragraph that follows describes a design in which the equality "directly supports" the assumption, but that design requires an external target-population adherence sample that is nowhere part of the data structure in \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array} (source (X,Z,D,Y) plus target X only). Fix: in Section 2, drop "standard" for this assumption, state plainly that it restricts the denominator of the estimand and is not implied by the observed two-sample structure, and rewrite the clinic paragraph to say that the external receipt data are a design device for justifying the assumption rather than an input the procedures use.

The finite-cell attainment results are presented as delivering feasible procedures that "learn the target weights from the target covariate sample" (abstract; introduction), but both constructions require substantial known structure that the prose underplays: \Cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} assumes the known equal cell masses 1/k_n and known propensity 1/2 via \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}, and \Cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} takes both (q_{x,n}) and (e_{x,n}) as known inputs to the procedure class \mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}. What is learned from the target sample is the cell frequency vector and the collision scale, not the density ratio in any generality. Fix: in the abstract sentence and in the introduction paragraph beginning "The feasible results replace oracle-known weights", state that the source cell partition, cell probabilities, and propensity remain known and that the target sample supplies the cell frequencies and the collision statistic \widehat\kappa_{U,n}.

\Cref{obj:ass:degrading-array} forces k_n \to \infty and \mu_n \to 0 into the definition of \mathcal P_n itself (\cref{obj:def:model-class}), which means every law in the model class is part of a degrading sequence and the fixed-n statements are statements about array rows, not about a fixed experiment. The paper never flags this; worse, \Cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction} imposes both k_n \to \infty and w_n \equiv 1, so the envelope scale diverges while the weights it envelopes are constant, making k_n a vestigial parameter in exactly the specialization offered as the reader's intuition anchor. Fix: add a remark after \cref{obj:def:model-class} noting that membership is a property of a triangular array row and that finite-n readings are asymptotic-sequence statements; and in the discussion after \Cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction}, note that under unit weights the envelope condition is inactive and is retained only for compatibility with \cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}.

Two definitions in Section 2 label the same object \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) — \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} ("Least-favorable witness") constructs the family, and \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} ("Geometry handle") reuses the identical notation while actually asserting the chi-square and total-variation inequalities \(1 + \chi^2 \le \exp(8t_0h^2)\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \le 2\rho\). Content that is proved is packaged as a definition, so the reader cannot tell what is stipulated and what is derived, and the duplicated name invites the reading that the second display defines rather than bounds. The Related Literature section states scope contrasts affirmatively in most places but the paragraph beginning "This positioning yields two direct scope statements" is thin on what is actually new relative to \citet{ChenHuang2025}, which is described as sharing the transported-CACE target, the two-sample generalizability design, and the transported compliance restrictions — i.e. the entire model. Abstract and introduction repeatedly use broad phrases such as “the oracle minimax expected-length frontier” and “attains this order”; revise these sentences to attach the exact domain each time, especially “over laws with t_n >= t_0,” oracle-known w and e, fixed positive t_0, and the overlap/envelope/degrading-array gates.

The related-literature section is accurate in broad strokes but too citation-dense; for each closest paper group, add one precise contrast tied to this paper’s formal object, such as compact ratio risk, effective strength n mu_n^2/kappa_n, or finite-cell target-weight learning.

The abstract and introduction assert a matched two-sided frontier for the full oracle class, but the theorems deliver only a one-sided pairing there: \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} obtains its lower bound by embedding the unit-weight (w=1, kappa_n=1) fixed geometry, which carries no covariate shift at all, while \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment} gives the upper bound. \cref{obj:ass:receipt-transport} is the paper's most consequential and least standard restriction, yet its supporting text calls it standard by citing \citet{ChenHuang2025} in the same one-line register used for randomization, exclusion, and monotonicity. Fix: promote this to its own subsection, drop the 'standard' framing, state explicitly which restrictions on the S=0 full-data law are identified by the observed samples and which are design assumptions supported by auxiliary evidence, and state what changes in \cref{obj:prop:compact-causal-range} if the averaged equality fails by a fixed amount.

The one-sentence justifications attached to \cref{obj:ass:population-presence,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination} all cite \citet{ChenHuang2025} and all begin with the word 'standard'. This makes the citation uninformative and misattributes classical LATE conditions (Imbens-Angrist, Angrist-Imbens-Rubin) and classical transport conditions (Cole-Stuart, Dahabreh et al.) to a single recent paper. Fix: route each assumption to its actual origin -- monotonicity and exclusion to \citet{ImbensAngrist1994,AngristImbensRubin1996}, support/positivity to \citet{ColeStuart2010,Dahabreh2020} -- and reserve the \citet{ChenHuang2025} citation for the transported-CACE restrictions it genuinely introduces; replace the repeated 'standard' with a substantive clause on what each condition rules out.

\cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class} reprints all fifteen conditions of \cref{obj:def:model-class} verbatim and then adds one, and \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} and \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} both define the same object Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g} under different names ('least-favorable witness' and 'geometry handle'), with \cref{obj:synth_5} restating the h=0 member a third time. A reader cannot tell whether these are distinct objects. Fix: replace the checklist in \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class} with 'P \in \mathcal P_n satisfying \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}' and move the audit list to the appendix; merge \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} into a lemma stating the chi-square and total-variation bounds for the family already defined in \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness}, and delete or fold in \cref{obj:synth_5}.

The bounded-outcome support in \cref{obj:ass:full-data-support} is what makes Theta=[-1,1] compact and therefore what makes min{1, t_0^{-1/2}} rather than an unbounded-length statement the right criterion, but the paper treats it as a technical normalization ('This support restriction is specific to this analysis'). The constant-length regime at small t_0 is entirely an artifact of the diameter of Theta, so the economic content of the frontier's flat portion is 'the parameter space is two units wide'. Fix: add a paragraph after \cref{obj:prop:compact-causal-range} discussing how the frontier constants scale with the outcome range, noting that for Y in [0,B] the flat portion is at height proportional to B, and stating which applications support a known bounded outcome scale.

The 'two direct scope statements' paragraph in the Related Literature section and the closing paragraph both restate the effective-strength summary already given in the introduction and at the end of Section 3, without adding a comparison a reader could check. Fix: cite the specific transported-ATE efficiency results being contrasted (e.g. \citet{Dahabreh2020,DahabrehPetitoRobertson2020}) and state the comparison as a displayed contrast of the two rate indices, then cut the redundant closing restatement.

\cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} is stated for the uniform-cell design with e(X)=1/2 and equal masses 1/k_n, but its proof (Steps 1-4) derives it as a corollary of \cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} with c_-=c_+=1 and an artificial overlap level \bar\varepsilon=1/4+a/2 constructed from c. claims_vs_assumptions: In the abstract and introduction, the oracle attainment is sometimes stated as holding over the transported class without foregrounding the theorem’s extra fixed/admissible-geometry and uniform-restriction gates; revise those summary sentences to mirror the exact hypotheses in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment}.

writing: The paper is clear and technically serious, but the introduction repeats the frontier formula and model gates several times; compress one repetition and use the space to preview the feasible/oracle distinction more sharply.

Array-level conditions are stated as row-level membership, leaving the central object ambiguous. \cref{obj:def:model-class} defines \(\mathcal P_n=\{(P_n^F,e):\ldots\text{satisfies the following conditions at index }n\}\), but three of the listed conditions (\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}'s \(N_n/n\to c\), \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}'s \(k_n\to\infty\), \(k_n=o(\sqrt n)\), \(\mu_n\to0\)) are limit statements that no single row can satisfy; the theorems then alternate between "\(P\in\mathcal P_n\)" and "every transported array \(P\)" (e.g. the hypotheses of \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} and \cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment}). Fix: define an admissible array \(\mathbf P=(P_n)_{n\ge1}\) once, carrying the schedules \((N_n,k_n,c,\varepsilon)\), and set \(\mathcal P_n=\{P_n:\mathbf P\text{ admissible}\}\); then say explicitly that the row supremum in \cref{obj:def:frontier-risk} ranges over rows of admissible arrays, so that \(t_n\ge t_0\) is a row condition while \(\mu_n\to0\) is an array condition.

The uniformity claim after \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} reads stronger than the witness supports. The sentence "the final uniformity clause indexes the lower bound by the combined effective strength uniformly over decompositions into first-stage weakness and weight dispersion" invites the reading that for each split of \(t_0\) into \((\mu_n,\kappa_n)\) there is a matching least-favorable law, whereas Steps 2--5 of the proof construct a single unit-weight geometry with \(\kappa_n=1\) and obtain the bound from \cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction}; the dispersion side of the claim is delivered separately by \cref{obj:thm:fixed-geometry-frontier}. Fix: replace that sentence with "the constants \(c_0,t_c\) are chosen before the array and depend on no feature of a row beyond \(t_n\ge t_0\); \cref{obj:thm:fixed-geometry-frontier} supplies matching witnesses at every admissible \((\kappa_n)\) schedule," and add the same pointer to the abstract sentence about the unit-transport-weight slice.

\cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} is a lemma presented as a definition, and the least-favorable law is defined three times. The environment titled "Geometry handle \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)" asserts \(1+\chi^2\le\exp(8t_0h^2)\) and \(\|Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}-Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le2\rho\) — substantive inequalities that carry the lower bound — while \cref{obj:synth_5}, \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness}, and \cref{obj:def:geometry-handle} all respecify the same compliance-type/Bernoulli-tilt construction. Fix: keep \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} as the sole definition (folding in the \(h=0\) member now isolated as \cref{obj:synth_5}), and restate the two separation bounds as a numbered lemma cited at Step 1 of the proof of \cref{obj:thm:fixed-geometry-frontier}.

The feasible finite-cell procedures are less sample-only than the abstract and \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-feasible-honesty} suggest. In \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} the critical constant \(L_{\alpha,c}=(2B_c/\alpha)^{1/2}\) with \(B_c=32(1+c^{-1})\) depends on the limit \(c=\lim N_n/n\), which is not a function of the sample, and \cref{obj:thm:regular-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} additionally takes the cell partition, the masses \((q_{x,n})\), and the propensities \((e_{x,n})\) as known inputs. Fix: in the implementation paragraph following \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment}, state the declared inputs as "target sample, source sample, known cell partition, known propensity, and the ratio constant \(c\)", and either note that any \(L\ge(2B_c/\alpha)^{1/2}\) works so that \(N_n/n\) may be substituted for \(c\) at the cost of a row-eventual statement, or say plainly that \(c\) is treated as design-known; correspondingly soften "learn the target weights from the target covariate sample" in the abstract to "learn the target cell weights, with the cell design and propensity known".

The relation to the classical unboundedness results for weakly identified ratios is never made explicit, although it is what makes the compact-\(\Theta\) formulation essential. \citet{GleserHwang1987} and \citet{Dufour1997} appear only inside citation lists in the Related Literature section and the appendix, yet the finite expected length in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment} rests entirely on intersecting the inversion set with \(\Theta=[-1,1]\), which \cref{obj:prop:compact-causal-range} justifies from bounded outcomes. Fix: add a paragraph to the weak-identification part of the Related Literature section stating that unbounded-parameter versions of this problem admit no honest bounded confidence set, and that the bounded-outcome support in \cref{obj:ass:full-data-support} is what converts the question into a well-posed expected-length problem; relatedly, "Kish-type dispersion" and "Kish dispersion" are used four times with no citation for the design-effect literature they invoke.

Assumption commentary is formulaic and mis-attributed, and the genuinely restrictive conditions get the least discussion. Nine consecutive one-sentence remarks call the condition "the standard ... condition \citep{ChenHuang2025}", attributing conditional randomization, exclusion, and monotonicity to a single recent paper rather than to \citet{ImbensAngrist1994} and \citet{AngristImbensRubin1996}; meanwhile the conditions specific to this analysis get one sentence each. In particular \cref{obj:ass:weight-second-moment} (\(\kappa_n\le k_n\)) is an additional restriction beyond the envelope \(w\le2k_n\) of \cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope} — it forces the weight distribution away from its most dispersed configurations — and \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array} makes \(\mu_n\to0\) and \(k_n\to\infty\) part of model membership, so the class excludes both strong identification and bounded covariate shift, which sits awkwardly with \cref{obj:prop:no-shift-reduction}'s unit-weight specialization. Fix: attribute each IV restriction to its canonical source, and add a short paragraph after \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array} interpreting \(\kappa_n\le k_n\) as an effective-sample-size floor \(n/\kappa_n\ge n/k_n\), stating what weight distributions saturate it, and explaining that \(\mu_n\to0\), \(k_n\to\infty\) is the drifting-sequence device that makes fixed-\(t_0\) asymptotics the relevant local comparison.

Two structural redundancies cost roughly two pages and blur the reader-facing statements. \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class} reprints all fifteen bullets of \cref{obj:def:model-class} to add one condition, even though the preceding sentence already gives the correct one-line definition \(\mathcal N_n=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}\}\); and the hypothesis bullets "(Transported-IV class.) Every array in \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfies [all fifteen assumptions]" in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} and "(Uniform model restrictions.)" in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment} restate the definition of the class as a hypothesis of the theorem. Fix: keep the one-line \(\mathcal N_n\) definition and delete the expanded environment; delete the tautological hypothesis bullets; and replace the opaque "(Admissible geometry.)" bullet and the following "The geometry clause therefore anchors the carrier structure" sentence with a plain statement that this hypothesis serves only to make \(\mathcal P_n\) eventually nonempty so the coverage infimum is not vacuous. Abstract and introduction repeatedly state the frontier as a broad characterization over transported triangular arrays, while several attainability and feasible statements require fixed overlap, bounded outcomes, k_n=o(sqrt n), known propensities, finite-cell structure, or admissible deterministic geometry; revise the opening contribution paragraph to list these gates in the same sentence as the frontier claim.

The two-sided characterization is order-only with an unexamined constant gap, and the paper never says so. In Section 3 ("Oracle Frontier and Score Inversion", the paragraph beginning "Combining \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse,obj:thm:oracle-score-inversion-attainment}") and in the abstract, the result is described as a matched frontier, but the lower constant is c_alpha = 3(1-alpha)^2/16 (about 0.18 at alpha=0.05) while the upper constant is C_alpha = max{2, 4L_alpha + 8/eps^2} with L_alpha = sqrt(8/(alpha eps^2)); at alpha=0.05, eps=0.1 this is roughly 1.3e3, so C_alpha*min{1,t_0^{-1/2}} exceeds the trivial length lambda(Theta)=2 unless t_0 is enormous. Fix: add a short remark after that paragraph giving the explicit ratio C_alpha/c_alpha, stating that the radius is Chebyshev-based and therefore conservative, and stating the range of t_0 over which the attainment bound improves on the trivial set Theta.

The converse in \cref{obj:thm:oracle-converse} is proved on a witness with unit transport weight (proof step 2 sets w_n == 1, e_n == 1/2, kappa_n = 1), yet the sentence following the theorem and the closing sentence of Section 3 ("The rate therefore treats a weak transported first stage and high transport dispersion symmetrically through n mu_n^2/kappa_n") reads as if dispersion itself has been shown to be binding, and the theorem's final clause ("The same constants c_0 and t_c apply uniformly over all decompositions of the effective strength t_0 into mu_n and kappa_n") invites the same over-reading. Fix: state plainly that the oracle converse is obtained by embedding the no-shift slice, attribute the dispersed-weight lower bound to \cref{obj:thm:fixed-geometry-frontier} (whose witness has p_n(x) proportional to w(x)), and reword the uniformity clause as "the constants do not depend on how t_0 is decomposed" rather than as a claim that every decomposition is separately witnessed.

Fix: keep \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-witness} as the construction (with the centered member named inline, deleting \cref{obj:synth_5}), and restate the two bounds as a lemma/proposition environment so cleveref reports "lemma" and the reader is not asked to accept an inequality as a naming convention.

Fix: amend the abstract sentence and the paragraph introducing \cref{obj:thm:finite-cell-unknown-weight-attainment} to say that the cell partition, source cell probabilities, and propensities are known design inputs and only the target cell frequencies and the collision scale are estimated; and add one sentence saying which construction, if any, is available for the general class P_n with continuous covariates, in an explicitly titled scope section.

Almost every standard IV restriction is annotated "this is the standard ... condition \citep{ChenHuang2025}" (the commentary after \cref{obj:ass:population-presence,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination}), which mis-attributes conditional randomization, exclusion, and monotonicity to a 2025 transport paper and makes the positioning read as citation-stuffing. There is no explicitly titled limitations or open-questions section and no numerical illustration, so genuine scope boundaries are dispersed into hedged clauses throughout Sections 3 and 4.
